content: Recent 2025-2026 decentralized-compute-verification research directly matches this project's use case: arxiv 2501.05374 trustless GPU validation uses probabilistic/consensus frameworks binary trusted-reference or ternary consensus rather than bit-exact recompute, because exact recomputation fails across GPU nodes; arxiv 2510.16028 TAO uses per-operator IEEE-754 worst-case error bounds tightened by empirical hardware-calibrated percentile profiles, accepting outputs within a derived tolerance region instead of quantizing/rounding the data itself, escalating to a Merkle-anchored dispute game on disagreement; arxiv 2606.00279 shows bitwise-exact reproduction is achievable without special hardware via software FP emulation matching the exact original kernel, but only within the same vendor path, not literally cross-vendor. Common thread: nobody quantizes-then-hashes at the field level in production-grade systems; they use scalar/derived-metric tolerance checks or graph-level dispute-resolution instead, because a single global rounding step cannot correctly handle mixed magnitudes across an entire tensor and is easy to game.
